title: Gram-Positive Resistance: Penicillinase, mecA/mecC, van Genes and HLAR
summary: Separate the resistance mechanisms of staphylococci and enterococci: blaZ penicillinase versus mecA/mecC PBP2a (and why cefoxitin is more reliable than oxacillin when mecC may be present), the vanA, vanB and vanC glycopeptide phenotypes, and high-level aminoglycoside resistance that ends synergy.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 58 Hits 6 (mecA/mecC), 8 (vanA/vanB/vanC) and 12 (high-level aminoglycoside resistance) and Exam Trap 3 (oxacillin-susceptible but penicillin-resistant S. aureus), checked against Lakhundi 2018 and Miller 2014 (both read via a page-fetch tool), Paterson 2014, Takayama 2018, O’Driscoll 2015, Shridhar 2019, Padmasini 2014 and Adhikari 2010. Qualifications taught from the sources: vanB vancomycin MICs range from 4 to 1,000 mg/L, so its marker is teicoplanin susceptibility rather than “lower-level” resistance; the streptomycin HLAR cutoff is method-dependent (>1,000 µg/mL broth, >2,000 µg/mL agar); most mecC MRSA tested on Vitek 2 are oxacillin susceptible but cefoxitin resistant, so oxacillin susceptibility does not by itself rule out methicillin resistance; nitrocefin is reported to be less sensitive than the penicillin zone-edge test. CLSI M100 itself was not read (paywalled); no breakpoint values beyond the screen concentrations are taught. Not taught: VISA/VRSA MIC cutoffs, public-health referral, infection-control handling of vanC.

objectives: Distinguish blaZ penicillinase from mecA/mecC PBP2a and predict which β-lactams each defeats.
Explain why cefoxitin is a more reliable marker than oxacillin or mecA-specific tests when mecC may be present.
Classify vanA, vanB and vanC enterococcal phenotypes by vancomycin and teicoplanin results.
Interpret a high-level gentamicin or streptomycin screen for synergy in enterococcal endocarditis.

scenes.title: Three Gram-positive puzzles
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three blood isolates. (1) Staphylococcus aureus: cefoxitin resistant, but mecA PCR and PBP2a latex both negative. (2) S. aureus: oxacillin susceptible, penicillin MIC in the susceptible range, but the penicillin zone has a sharp edge. (3) Enterococcus from a patient with endocarditis: vancomycin resistant, teicoplanin susceptible, and it grows on the high-level gentamicin screen. Question token: “What does each result mean for the report?”

cues.text: Three blood isolates. A Staphylococcus aureus that is cefoxitin resistant, yet negative for mecA and for PBP2a.
A second Staphylococcus aureus is oxacillin susceptible with a susceptible penicillin MIC, but its penicillin zone has a sharp edge.
And an endocarditis enterococcus that is vancomycin resistant, teicoplanin susceptible, and grows on the high-level gentamicin screen. What does each result mean?

scenes.title: Two ways S. aureus beats β-lactams
scenes.altText: Schematic: two cards. Penicillinase card: blaZ encodes a penicillinase (a class A β-lactamase) that hydrolyses the β-lactam ring of penicillin; it is often plasmid-borne. Oxacillin and other penicillinase-stable agents are not destroyed by it. PBP2a card: mecA, carried on the mobile SCCmec element, encodes PBP2a, an extra penicillin-binding protein with low affinity for β-lactams, giving resistance to essentially the whole β-lactam class except the anti-MRSA cephalosporins ceftaroline and ceftobiprole. mecC token: a mecA homologue only about 69% identical at the DNA level; mecA PCR and PBP2a latex tests miss it. Detection token: cefoxitin is more reliable than oxacillin for detecting methicillin resistance.

cues.text: Staphylococcus aureus has two separate tricks against beta-lactams. The first is penicillinase, made by the blaZ gene. It cuts the beta-lactam ring of penicillin, but not of oxacillin.
The second is PBP2a, made by mecA on the mobile SCCmec cassette. PBP2a barely binds beta-lactams, so the cell keeps building its wall. That is methicillin resistance, or MRSA.
PBP2a defeats essentially every beta-lactam. The exceptions are the anti-MRSA cephalosporins, ceftaroline and ceftobiprole.
A cousin gene, mecC, is only about sixty-nine percent identical to mecA, so mecA PCR and PBP2a latex tests miss it. Cefoxitin detects methicillin resistance more reliably than oxacillin.

props.title: mecC (~69% like mecA)
lines: Missed by mecA PCR · PBP2a latex

scenes.title: Vancomycin resistance in enterococci
scenes.altText: Schematic: the cell-wall precursor ends in D-Ala-D-Ala, the vancomycin binding site. Three gene cards (O’Driscoll 2015, Table 1; Miller 2014). VanA: precursor changed to D-Ala-D-Lac (about 1,000-fold lower vancomycin affinity); vancomycin MIC 64–1,000 mg/L and teicoplanin MIC 16–512 mg/L; transferable; most human VRE, mostly E. faecium. VanB: also D-Ala-D-Lac; vancomycin MIC variable, 4–1,000 mg/L; teicoplanin stays susceptible (0.5–1 mg/L). VanC: D-Ala-D-Ser (about 7-fold lower affinity); low-level vancomycin MIC 2–32 mg/L; teicoplanin susceptible; intrinsic, chromosomal, not transferable, in E. gallinarum and E. casseliflavus. Token: vanA has moved from VRE into MRSA, producing vancomycin-resistant S. aureus.

cues.text: Vancomycin and teicoplanin grab the D-alanine, D-alanine end of the cell-wall building block. Resistant enterococci rebuild that end.

vanA swaps the last alanine for lactate. Vancomycin binds about a thousand times less well, so resistance is high level, and teicoplanin fails too. vanA is transferable and causes most human VRE, mostly Enterococcus faecium.
vanB makes the same lactate swap, but teicoplanin stays active. Its vancomycin MICs vary widely, from low to very high.

vanC uses serine instead, giving only low-level vancomycin resistance. It is intrinsic, built into the chromosome of Enterococcus gallinarum and casseliflavus, and does not transfer. vanA, by contrast, has jumped into MRSA to make vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

props.label: Target: D-Ala-D-Ala end of the wall precursor

scenes.title: High-level aminoglycoside screen, then the answers
scenes.altText: Synergy card: enterococci are intrinsically tolerant of aminoglycosides at low levels (poor uptake); a cell-wall-active drug (ampicillin, or vancomycin) helps the aminoglycoside enter, giving bactericidal synergy for endocarditis. High-level resistance (HLAR) abolishes that synergy. Screen card: gentamicin 500 µg/mL; streptomycin >1,000 µg/mL by broth dilution or >2,000 µg/mL by agar dilution (screen concentrations depend on method). The bifunctional enzyme AAC(6′)-Ie-APH(2″)-Ia confers resistance to all aminoglycosides except streptomycin, so streptomycin is screened separately. Hook answers: (1) cefoxitin R, mecA and PBP2a negative → suspect mecC MRSA, report as methicillin resistant and confirm with a method that detects mecC; (2) sharp zone edge → suggests penicillinase, so penicillin cannot be relied on even though oxacillin is susceptible; (3) vanco R, teico S → vanB-type pattern (or vanC if the species is E. gallinarum or E. casseliflavus); gentamicin will not provide synergy — check streptomycin.

cues.text: Enterococci shrug off low levels of aminoglycosides because the drug gets in poorly. A cell-wall drug, such as ampicillin, opens the way, and together they kill. That synergy matters in endocarditis.

High-level aminoglycoside resistance destroys the synergy. The screen uses five hundred micrograms per millilitre of gentamicin. For streptomycin, the cutoff depends on the method: one thousand in broth, two thousand in agar.
The common gentamicin-modifying enzyme spares streptomycin, so streptomycin is screened separately and may still work.

The answers. Isolate one: suspect mecC MRSA and report it as methicillin resistant. Isolate two: the sharp edge suggests penicillinase, so penicillin cannot be relied on. Isolate three: a vanB-type pattern, and gentamicin cannot give synergy, so check streptomycin.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Oxacillin susceptible rules out MRSA” (✓ on the Vitek 2 system most mecC MRSA test cefoxitin resistant but oxacillin susceptible; cefoxitin is the more reliable marker); “Oxacillin susceptible means penicillin susceptible” (✓ blaZ penicillinase destroys penicillin but not oxacillin; check penicillin with a zone-edge test, not nitrocefin alone); “Vancomycin resistant + teicoplanin susceptible = vanA” (✓ vanA gives teicoplanin resistance; teicoplanin-susceptible VRE fits vanB, or vanC in E. gallinarum or E. casseliflavus).

cues.text: Trap one: an oxacillin-susceptible result rules out MRSA. No: on one automated system, most mecC strains tested oxacillin susceptible but cefoxitin resistant. Trust cefoxitin.
Trap two: oxacillin susceptible means penicillin susceptible. No: penicillinase destroys penicillin but spares oxacillin. Check with a zone-edge test, because nitrocefin alone can miss it.
Trap three: vancomycin resistant with teicoplanin susceptible means vanA. No: vanA knocks out teicoplanin too. That pattern fits vanB, or vanC in gallinarum or casseliflavus.

props.title: ✗ “Oxacillin S rules out MRSA.”
lines: ✓ mecC: often oxacillin S, cefoxitin R

props.title: ✗ “Vanco R + teico S = vanA.”
lines: ✓ vanA kills teicoplanin too: think vanB or vanC

scenes.title: Shredder, new lock, new keyhole, tagger
scenes.altText: Memory aid: four tokens. SHREDDER = blaZ penicillinase destroys the penicillin key. NEW LOCK = mecA/mecC PBP2a ignores β-lactam keys. NEW KEYHOLE = vanA/vanB/vanC reshape the D-Ala-D-Ala end that glycopeptides grab. TAGGER = an aminoglycoside-modifying enzyme tags the drug, ending synergy. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the shredder is penicillinase, destroying the penicillin key. The new lock is PBP2a, which beta-lactam keys no longer fit. The new keyhole is the reshaped wall end that vancomycin cannot grab. The tagger is the enzyme that marks aminoglycosides, ending synergy.

Where it breaks: ceftaroline and ceftobiprole still fit the new lock; the mecC lock is shaped differently, so mecA tests miss it; vanB keyholes still admit teicoplanin; and vanC is a keyhole the species was born with.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: mecC lock: mecA tests miss it

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Penicillinase spares oxacillin · PBP2a (mecA/mecC) beats all β-lactams but ceftaroline and ceftobiprole · cefoxitin detects it best”, “vanA = vancomycin + teicoplanin R · vanB = teicoplanin S · vanC = intrinsic · HLAR = no synergy”.

cues.text: In Gram-positive cocci, penicillinase destroys penicillin but spares oxacillin, PBP2a from mecA or mecC defeats nearly every beta-lactam and is caught more reliably with cefoxitin than with oxacillin, vanA removes both glycopeptides while vanB spares teicoplanin, and high-level aminoglycoside resistance ends synergy.

props.label: Penicillinase spares oxacillin · PBP2a → cefoxitin R
vanA: vanco + teico R · vanB: teico S · HLAR: no synergy

explanation.what: Plain language: staphylococci and enterococci beat common antibiotics in a few distinct ways. S. aureus can make an enzyme that destroys penicillin, or a new wall-building protein that ignores almost all penicillin-like drugs. Enterococci can rebuild the spot vancomycin grabs, and can carry enzymes that disable aminoglycosides. Scientific terms: blaZ penicillinase (class A β-lactamase), mecA and mecC, SCCmec, PBP2a, cefoxitin surrogate, D-Ala-D-Ala, D-Ala-D-Lac, D-Ala-D-Ser, vanA/vanB/vanC, teicoplanin, intrinsic versus acquired resistance, high-level aminoglycoside resistance (HLAR), AAC(6′)-Ie-APH(2″)-Ia, bactericidal synergy.
explanation.why: Each mechanism predicts a different reporting pattern. Penicillinase removes penicillin but leaves penicillinase-stable drugs; PBP2a removes essentially every β-lactam except the anti-MRSA cephalosporins; vanA removes both glycopeptides whereas vanB leaves teicoplanin; HLAR removes the aminoglycoside partner needed for bactericidal endocarditis therapy.
explanation.measure: S. aureus: cefoxitin is more reliable than oxacillin for methicillin resistance; mecA PCR and PBP2a latex miss mecC; guidelines recommend the penicillin zone-edge test (a sharp edge suggests penicillinase) and nitrocefin, nitrocefin being reported less sensitive. Enterococci (O’Driscoll 2015 Table 1): vanA vancomycin 64–1,000 mg/L, teicoplanin 16–512; vanB vancomycin 4–1,000, teicoplanin 0.5–1; vanC vancomycin 2–32, teicoplanin 0.5–1. HLAR screen: gentamicin 500 µg/mL; streptomycin >1,000 µg/mL broth or >2,000 µg/mL agar.
explanation.differs: Penicillinase (destroys penicillin) vs PBP2a (target bypass); mecA vs mecC (detection gap); vanA (teicoplanin R, transferable) vs vanB (teicoplanin S) vs vanC (intrinsic, low-level, E. gallinarum/E. casseliflavus); low-level intrinsic aminoglycoside tolerance vs acquired high-level resistance.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: name the gene from a vancomycin/teicoplanin pattern, explain an oxacillin-susceptible but penicillin-resistant S. aureus, choose cefoxitin as the MRSA marker, or state what a positive high-level gentamicin screen means for endocarditis therapy.

questions.stem: A Staphylococcus aureus blood isolate is cefoxitin resistant, but mecA PCR and a PBP2a latex test are both negative. What is the best explanation?

options.text: A mecC-carrying MRSA that mecA-specific tests do not detect
options.rationale: Correct. mecC is only about 69% identical to mecA, so mecA PCR and PBP2a latex miss it, while cefoxitin resistance still shows.

options.text: A methicillin-susceptible isolate; report β-lactams as susceptible
options.rationale: Incorrect. Cefoxitin resistance is the more reliable marker; negative mecA-specific tests do not exclude mecC.
Incorrect. Penicillinase hydrolyses penicillin; cefoxitin resistance is the marker used for PBP2a-mediated methicillin resistance.
Incorrect. vanA alters the glycopeptide target and does not cause β-lactam resistance.

questions.stem: An Enterococcus faecalis isolate from endocarditis is ampicillin susceptible and grows on the 500 µg/mL high-level gentamicin screen; the streptomycin screen shows no high-level resistance. What does this mean?

options.text: Gentamicin cannot provide synergy, but streptomycin may still
options.rationale: Correct. High-level resistance abolishes synergy for that drug; the common gentamicin-modifying enzyme spares streptomycin, which is tested separately.

options.text: All aminoglycosides, including streptomycin, will fail
options.rationale: Incorrect. Streptomycin is screened separately because the bifunctional gentamicin enzyme does not affect it.
Incorrect. The aminoglycoside screen does not change ampicillin’s activity; bactericidal killing came from the combination.

options.text: Growth on the screen is expected intrinsic low-level resistance and can be ignored
options.rationale: Incorrect. Intrinsic tolerance is low level; growth at 500 µg/mL gentamicin is acquired high-level resistance.

questions.stem: An Enterococcus faecium isolate has a vancomycin MIC of 256 mg/L and a teicoplanin MIC of 64 mg/L. Which gene best explains this pattern?

options.rationale: Correct. vanA gives high-level resistance to both vancomycin and teicoplanin and is mostly found in E. faecium.
Incorrect. vanB isolates typically remain teicoplanin susceptible.
Incorrect. vanC gives low-level vancomycin resistance (2–32 mg/L), teicoplanin susceptibility, and belongs to E. gallinarum and E. casseliflavus.
Incorrect. mecA encodes PBP2a and causes β-lactam resistance in staphylococci, not glycopeptide resistance.

claims.text: mecA on SCCmec encodes low-affinity PBP2a; resistance to essentially all β-lactams except ceftaroline and ceftobiprole.
mecC ~69% identical to mecA; missed by mecA PCR and PBP2a latex; cefoxitin more reliable than oxacillin; most mecC MRSA cefoxitin R but oxacillin S on Vitek 2.

blaZ penicillinase destroys penicillin but not oxacillin; oxacillin-susceptible S. aureus can be penicillin resistant; sharp zone edge suggests penicillinase; nitrocefin reported less sensitive than zone-edge.
vanA/vanB/vanC precursor changes, MIC ranges, teicoplanin results, transferability and species; vanA transfer to MRSA.

Intrinsic low-level aminoglycoside tolerance, synergy with cell-wall agents, loss of synergy with HLAR; gentamicin 500 µg/mL; streptomycin >1,000 broth / >2,000 agar; bifunctional enzyme spares streptomycin.
Exact current CLSI M100 reporting rules and breakpoints for these organisms (M100 not read; paywalled). Not taught beyond the screen concentrations reported by the cited sources.
Reviewer’s “never panic over vanC” (infection-control handling of vanC isolates): no open source read; not taught.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 58 Hit 8 calls vanB “lower-level vancomycin resistance”. O’Driscoll 2015 (Table 1) gives VanB vancomycin MICs of 4–1,000 mg/L; the reliable distinguisher from vanA is teicoplanin susceptibility, not the vancomycin level.

Ch. 58 Hit 12 gives a single streptomycin screen of 1,000 µg/mL. The cutoff is method-dependent: >1,000 µg/mL by broth dilution and >2,000 µg/mL by agar dilution (Shridhar 2019, citing CLSI; Adhikari 2010 agar screen 2,000 µg/mL).

Ch. 58 Exam Trap 3 says oxacillin susceptibility “only rules out mecA”. Paterson 2014 reports that on the Vitek 2 system most mecC MRSA are cefoxitin resistant but oxacillin susceptible, and that cefoxitin is more reliable than oxacillin; oxacillin susceptibility alone does not exclude methicillin resistance.

Ch. 58 Hit 6 says to screen penicillin-susceptible S. aureus with nitrocefin. Takayama 2018 notes CLSI/EUCAST recommend nitrocefin and the penicillin zone-edge test and that nitrocefin is reported less sensitive than zone-edge (in that study only 2 of 200 MSSA were blaZ positive, and both nitrocefin and zone-edge tests performed poorly: nitrocefin sensitivity 50%, P10 zone-edge PPV 18.2%). See also register flag rv-nitrocefin.
